entry.title: What Apple's Q4 2026 record taught me about my own numbers
entry.content:
I read Apple's Q4 2026 earnings the way I read my own studio's books: looking for the line nobody wants to talk about. My studio is tiny, and I still learned more from their $114.5 billion than from a year of my own spreadsheets.

The record that wasn't the point

Everyone led with the iPhone record. I kept looking at the services line, because that's the part of my own work I keep underpricing.1

Revenue is a story you tell about last quarter. Margin is the one you tell about next year.

Three things I'm changing:

  • I'm pricing repairs by the hour, not by the bowl.
  • I'm writing down every job I turn away.
  • I'm keeping a plain list of what each piece cost me:
    1. materials
    2. time
    3. the second coat nobody sees

The spreadsheet formula I use now is one line:

=SUM(materials) + hours * rate

That's all. Read my older post on pricing for the long version.

  1. My services line is teaching, and I charge too little for it. ↩

entry.title: Mending a bowl, slowly
entry.content:
I spent my weekend mending a cracked bowl. My hands still smell of lacquer, and I liked every hour of it.

The third coat is the one I always want to skip.

entry.title: Notes from the workbench
entry.content: I keep a notebook beside the bench. My rule: if I fix it twice, I write it down.
